This request gets information such as Bill IDs, Bill Numbers, etc.

This call returns a "meta" object containing URLs that can be used to get data related to the Bill.

Note: this endpoint supports pagination. Please refer to the [**Pagination**](#pagination) section for more information.

Return data description

Property: meta, Description: useful links relating to this Bill
Property: billID, Description: The unique ID of the Bill.
Property: billNumber, Description: The bill number assigned to the Bill.
Property: poID, Description: The poID of which the Bill was made.
Property: locationID, Description: The unique ID of the location associated with this Bill.
Property: date, Description: The date this Bill was created as a UNIX timestamp.
Property: status, Description: The status of this Bill. The status can be as follows: 0: The bill is setup. 1: The bill is submitted. 2: The bill is closed i.e. Marked as Paid
Property: userID, Description: The Id of the user this Bill was assigned to.
Property: userIDStarted, Description: The ID of the user this Bill was created by.
Property: userIDMarkPaid, Description: The ID of the user this Bill was marked paid by.

info.name: Limble API V2 Assets Bills API

description.content:
Getting Started!

Welcome to Limble CMMS’s API documentation.

You can use this documentation to configure connections to the Limble CMMS API over https using RESTful standards.

Using the API you can get information about the following portions of your system:

- Assets

- Locations

- Parts (Current quantities and Usage)

- Tasks (Work Orders, Preventive Maintenance, Work Requests, etc.)

- Users

- Vendors

- Roles

- Teams

- Purchase Orders

- General Ledgers

- Budgets

- Priorities

- Tags

- Statuses

- Bills

- Regions

- Webhooks

- Units of Measure(UOM)

Please use the correct Limble API URL to connect to our API based on the region or the type of your Limble Account.

| **Limble Account (Region/Type)** | **Limble API URL** |
| --- | --- |
| Default | api.limblecmms.com |
| Canada | ca-api.limblecmms.com |
| Australia | au-api.limblecmms.com |
| Europe | eu-api.limblecmms.com |
| 21CFR | 21cfr-api.limblecmms.com |

---

# Authentication

To protect your information the Limble CMMS API uses BASIC authorization standards.

Every call to the API must include an authorization header with your base 64 encoded id and secret.

Client ID

Your Client ID is your unique customer identification.

Client Secret

Your Client Secret is used to authenticate the Client ID on each API call. This is something that must be kept secret.

> How do I get my Client ID and Client Secret? 

To obtain your Client ID and Client Secret login to your Limble account as a **Super Administrator** and go to **Settings** -> **Configuration**, on this page scroll down to the **API Settings** section and click **Generate API Keys**. Keep this information **secret**, you will only be able to see your Client Secret once upon initial generation. If you lose your secret you will need to regenerate it and update your integration accordingly.

> Example Header 
Authorization: Basic \[BASE64 ENCODED YOUR_CLIENT_ID:YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET 

Below is a code example for PHP:

```
$curl = curl_init();
$id = 'your_client_id';
$secret = 'your_client_id';
$headers = array(
'Content-Type:application/json',
'Authorization: Basic '. base64_encode($id.':'.$secret)
);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);
curl_setopt_array($curl, array(
CURLOPT_URL => 'https://api.limblecmms.com:443/v2/tasks/',
CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
CURLOPT_ENCODING => "",
CURLOPT_MAXREDIRS => 10,
CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 0,
CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION => false,
CURLOPT_HTTP_VERSION => CURL_HTTP_VERSION_1_1,
CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => "GET",
));
$response = curl_exec($curl);
$err = curl_error($curl);
curl_close($curl);
if ($err) {
echo "cURL Error #:" . $err;
} else {
echo $response;
} ?>

```

Below is a code example for NodeJS:

```
const https = require('https');
const id = 'your_client_id';
const secret = 'your_client_secret';
const options = {
'method': 'GET',
'hostname': 'api.limblecmms.com',
'path': '/v2/tasks/?',
'headers': {
'Authorization': 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${credentials.id}:${credentials.secret}`).toString('base64')
}
};
const req = https.request(options, function (res) {
const chunks = [];
res.on("data", function (chunk) {
chunks.push(chunk);
});
res.on("end", function (chunk) {
const body = Buffer.concat(chunks);
console.log(body.toString());
});
res.on("error", function (error) {
console.error(error);
});
});
req.end();

```

---

# Error Codes

- HTTP 400 - Data Validation Error - Malformed JSON input or incorrect data type.

- HTTP 403 - Forbidden - The resource cannot be accessed.

- HTTP 404 - Resource not found - The resource you are targeting does not exist.

- HTTP 409 - Resource Conflict - A resource already exists with those parameters.

- HTTP 422 - Unprocessable Entity - The syntax of the request is correct but cannot be processed due to semantic errors.

- HTTP 429 - Too Many Requests - See the rate limiting section below.

- HTTP 500 - Internal Server Error - Contact Limble for assistance.

- HTTP 501 - Method Not Support - Limble's API only supports GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, and DELETE.

---

# Success Codes

- HTTP 200 - OK - Everything was successful. PUTs, PATCHs and DELETEs on success always return an empty 200 OK.

- HTTP 201 - CREATED - This is used on POST calls when new resouces are created. If a new resource was created Limble will always pass back a GET URL in the location header so a developer can easily GET the new resource.

# Overriding HTTP methods

Some systems may support only the `POST` and `GET` HTTP methods. This restriction prevents using other HTTP methods such as `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`. RESTful web API implementations can work around this restriction by letting the client override the HTTP method via the custom HTTP headers.

The Limble API supports **Method Overrides** by using a `POST` request and setting the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header with a method string value. The header value can be `PATCH` or `PUT`. This will allow Limble API users to use `PATCH` and `PUT` endpoints by sending `POST` requests to these endpoints and overriding them with the respective HTTP method.

# Webhooks

Receive data on certain events such as Tasks being completed.

Limble's webhooks allow you to receive data whenever specific events occur.

For example, you may need to run your own script whenever a Task is completed.

Limble supports adding multiple webhooks that can be triggered when actions are carried out on:

- Tasks

- Assets

- Asset Fields

- Purchase Orders

- Purchase Order Items

When an event occurs, Limble sends an HTTP POST request to a URL endpoint you configure.

You can configure this URL in the Limble Web App under:

**Settings → Configuration → API Settings**

All data sent is JSON-encoded, and Limble includes the following fields in the request headers for validation:

- `signature`

- `timestamp`

- `token`

You may register multiple webhooks for the same event type.

### Important: API Key Requirement for Webhooks

To receive webhooks, the customer must have at least one active **limbleAPI key** created in API Settings.

- Webhooks **will not function** without at least one valid `limbleAPI` key.

- Limble uses the **first-created** **`limbleAPI`** **key** (by creation date) to generate the **signature** included in webhook headers.

- The receiving system must use this key to verify the authenticity of incoming webhook requests.

If a customer has multiple `limbleAPI` keys, **only the oldest one** will be used for signing webhook requests.

### Response Time and Retry Behavior

Your server must respond to webhook POST requests within **10 seconds**.

If it does not, Limble will attempt to retry the webhook request.

Limble handles server responses as follows:

- If the server returns **200 OK**, Limble considers the webhook successful and will not retry.

- If the server returns **406 Not Acceptable**, Limble considers the webhook received but intentionally ignored — no retry will occur.

- For any other response (e.g., 500, timeout, etc.), Limble will retry the request.

**Retry schedule:**

- After 10 minutes

- After 1 hour

- After 2 hours

- After 4 hours

After the final retry attempt, the webhook will be **automatically disabled**.

### Re-enabling a Disabled Webhook

To re-enable a disabled webhook:

1. Go to **Settings → Configuration → API Settings** in the Limble Web App. 
Find the webhook and use the option to **Re-enable** the API endpoint.

2. Alternatively, send a `PATCH` request using the **Update Webhook** endpoint and set `enabled = true`.

### Assets

Below is an example payload you might be sent when an event occurs on an asset:

```
{
"assetID": 10748, 
"status": "CREATED",
"category": "asset", 
"user": "bob@limblecmms.com" 
}

```

Once the Payload is received you can use the Get Assets API call to get the most recent Asset data. The following is a list of all the possible statuses that a webhook might be set to:

CREATED | An Asset is created
DELETED | An Asset was deleted
CHANGED ASSET NAME | An asset has been renamed

## Securing Webhooks

To ensure the authenticity and integrity of webhook events each webhook is 
signed with a signature as well as some other data described below:

timestamp | int | A standard unix time stamp
token | string | , randomly generated string that is an integrity check of the, payload.,
signature | String | A string generated by the HMAC algorithm

To verify the webhook is originating from LimbleCMMS you will need to:

- Concatenate the timestamp and token

- Encode your private API key (oldest Limble API Key) with the SHA256 algorithm

- Encode the timestamp and token value with the HMAC algorithm using your hashed private key and the SHA256 method.

- Compare the resulting digest to the signature provided in your webhook 
header

## Validation Code Examples

Code samples to verify webhook data.

PHP

```
function verify($timestamp, $signature, $apiKey, $token)
//hash private key
$apiKey = hash('sha256', $apiKey);
$generated_signature = hash_hmac('sha256', $timestamp . $token, $apiKey);
if($generated_signature === $signature) {
return true;
} else {
return false;
}
} 

```

NodeJS

```
var crypto = require('crypto');
const verify = (apiKey, token, timestamp, signature) => {
//hash private key
const apiKey = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(apiKey).digest('hex');
const value = timestamp+token;
const generated_signature = crypto.createHmac('sha256',apiKey).update(value).digest('hex');
if(signature === generated_signature){
return true;
} else {
return false;
}
};

```

# Rate limit

To help protect against run-away scripts, clients who make an inordinate 
number of calls over a period of time may be temporarily blocked from 
accessing the service. The limits are defined in the table below. If you 
receive an error indicating that you have exceeded the call limit, please 
wait and try again later. If you need higher limits please reach out to your dedicated account manager.

## Per Hour

GET | 4000 calls per hour. | 360 calls per minute.
PATCH | 2000 calls per hour. | 240 calls per minute.
POST | 1000 calls per hour. | 240 calls per minute.
PUT | 1000 calls per hour. | 240 calls per minute.
DELETE | 100 calls per hour. | 60 calls per minute.
BATCH REQUEST | 20 calls per hour | 5 calls per minute

Every API response is accompanied by the following set of headers to identify the status of your consumption. API calls are rate-limited on two windows of time: per-minute and per-hour. For example, if you made a request at 13:42:42, that request will expire from your per-minute window at 13:43:42 and from your per-hour window at 14:42:42.

X-RateLimit-Limit | The maximum number of requests that the consumer is permitted to make per hour.
X-RateLimit-Remaining | The number of requests remaining in the current per-hour window.
X-RateLimit-First-Call | The time your first call was made in the current per-hour window.
X-RateLimit-TTL | The time until more request resources become available (This only displays when you've hit your limit).
X-RateLimit-Minute-Limit | The maximum number of requests that the consumer is permitted to make per minute.
X-RateLimit-Minute-Remaining | The number of requests remaining in the current per-minute window.
X-RateLimit-Minute-First-Call | The time your first call was made in the current per-minute window.
X-RateLimit-Minute-TTL | The time until more request resources become available (This only displays when you've hit your limit).

# Pagination

Currently pagination using OrderBy and cursor is supported only by **GET Tasks** and **GET Assets**. Pagination using Limit and Page is supported by many other GET endpoints including **GET Tasks** and **GET Assets**.

Pagination can be implemented by using the orderBy, cursor, limit and page query parameters. 
**Note: cursor and page cannot be used simultaneously for pagination.**

## Pagination using Limit and Page

This uses limit and page query parameters. For a given limit and page results will be paginated. If orderBy query parameter is given the results will be ordered and paginated accordingly.

The page parameter is **required** and can be greater than or equal to 1 for this pagination method. The default limit is 100 but can be changed. The max limit is 1000.

The response headers contain information about the Previous, Next and Last Page of the result based on the limit.

The result will be empty when for a given limit, the given page does not exist. For example, if there are 100 Assets in total and limit is set at 10, only pages 1-10 are possible. An empty result will be given for page numbers greater than 10.

This pagination method is supported by various GET endpoints. Please refer to the examples for those GET endpoints for more information.

## Pagination using OrderBy and Cursor

**Note**: If you're implementing pagination for the first time for **GET Tasks** or **GET Assets** please follow **Pagination Using Limit and Page** as the use of **Cursor** will be deprecated in the next API version.

This uses orderBy and cursor query parameters. Generally, in all of our GET endpoints, the cursor parameter ensures that the ID will be greater than the value of cursor. This makes sense when we're ordering the results ascending by ID.

In GET Assets, when we're fetching a set of assets and ordering by lastEdited (ascending) or -lastEdited (descending), the cursor parameter will instead ensure that we're returning a set of results that begin at the next asset in the order, regardless of whether its **ID is greater or less than the value of cursor**.

If the value of cursor does not match an existing assetID, then the result set will be empty, because there is no lastEdited value to compare to. **When providing orderBy and cursor, the value of cursor must be a real assetID or the result set will be empty.**

The same applies for GET Tasks when using cursor and ordering by createdDate, dateCompleted and due.
